subject: Reserved commit ladder + safety corridor proposal / GPU pass-through mechanics
messages:
From: Alex Dunham <alex.dunham@edgescale.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity ask — thinking about price protection mechanics

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week. EdgeScale is excited about Redwood Dedicated — the latency profile looks like a good fit for our real-time inference needs. We are heading into procurement and want to discuss a reserved capacity proposal.

A couple of asks from our side:
- We need a multi-tranche commit over 24 months (phased activation).
- We want a "safety corridor" so that if GPU market costs spike >15% we can trigger a partial decommit window or a shared-cost pass-through (we are open to some cost-sharing).
- Can you sketch how discounts/credits would be applied if market GPU prices fall (rebates) vs rise (pass-through)?

Could someone from your pricing or finance team sketch scenarios (5%, 15%, 30% swings) and the quickest approval path for an exception to standard commit discounts?

Alex
Alex Dunham
Head of Platform Partnerships, EdgeScale
+1 (415) 555-0192

--

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dunham <alex.dunham@edgescale.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — thinking about price protection mechanics

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Marissa (deals) and Karthik (pricing/finance) to model scenarios. Initial thoughts:

- We can structure a commit ladder (tranches at months 0, 6, 12, 18) with an option to rebalance capacity at the 12-month mark.
- For downside (market price drop) we typically provide retrospective credits applied to ongoing consumption credits on a quarterly cadence.
- For upside risk (price rise), we can do two patterns: a) limited pass-through up to a cap (shared-cost corridor) or b) a decommit window triggered at a threshold. Each has different discount impacts.

Marissa and Karthik — can you prepare a short scenario table (5/15/30% GPU cost delta) showing effective per-token/unit price under: baseline discount, safety-corridor shared pass-through, and decommit-plus-credit? Also what approval tier is needed for an ad hoc pass-through above standard terms?

Alex — planning to get you a sketch within 36 hours. Would a quick call Thurs morning work to walk through the numbers?

Thanks,
Sean
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — thinking about price protection mechanics

Adding Monica from commercial ops for operational constraints. Draft scenario table attached (20261028-commit-ladder-term-sheet.xlsx) and a short safety_corridor-draft.pdf with proposed trigger language. Key points from our side:

- Commit ladder: 25% / 25% / 25% / 25% activation over 24 months. Rebalance option at month 12 with 45-day notice.
- Pricing: baseline discount tier A = 30% off list for committed pool. If GPU market cost rises >15% vs base, trigger a safety corridor where cost increase is shared 50/50 up to a 30% increase. Above 30% it's an exec escalation for credit or decommit.
- Approval path: discounts up to 35% are finance-level; any shared-cost pass-through that increases customer-priced units requires CS + Finance + Revenue Ops sign-off; >20% effective increase needs VP/GM approval.

Open items before we present to EdgeScale:
1) Do we want a quarterly reconciliation (credits) or monthly for this account? (monthly better for EdgeScale cashflow but operational heavier)
2) Do we allow a one-time partial decommit at month 12 against future credits (yes/no)?

If no objections, I'll convert the doc to a customer-facing term sheet.

- Marissa
Senior Director, Deals — Redwood Inference

--

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — thinking about price protection mechanics

Quick numbers attached in the spreadsheet (tab: sensitivity_summary). Highlights (rounded):
- Baseline unit cost (internal GPU input) = $0.85/token-equivalent
- Baseline customer price after 30% commit discount = $0.595/unit

Scenario (customer effective price):
- GPU +5% => internal 0.892 => no pass-through under corridor => customer price remains $0.595 (we absorb up to 5%)
- GPU +15% => internal 0.977 => shared 50/50 => customer pays + 0.065 => effective customer price ~ $0.660 (+11%)
- GPU +30% => internal 1.105 => shared 50/50 up to 30% cap => customer pays +0.13 => effective customer price ~ $0.725 (+22%); above this threshold we'd route to execs for guidance.

Approval timing: finance can sign off on corridor language and up to 12% uplift to effective customer price (routine). Anything that materially exceeds that (20%+) needs VP sign-off and legal for contract language on triggers.

Operational note: monthly reconciliation would require small changes to billing pipeline and we'd need a 2-week lead time to operationalize. Recommend quarterly to start and transition to monthly within 2 quarters if EdgeScale prefers.

-Karthik
Head of Pricing & Revenue Strategy

--

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dunham <alex.dunham@edgescale.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 15:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — thinking about price protection mechanics

Alex — attaching the term sheet and sensitivity tab for your review (see attachments). Short summary of our offer:

1) Commit ladder: tranche activation across 24 months with 12-month rebalance window.
2) Discount: 30% baseline on committed pool.
3) Safety corridor: for GPU cost increases between 15–30%, we propose a shared-cost pass-through (50/50). For increases >30% we trigger an executive review with options for partial decommit or expanded shared-cost.
4) Reconciliations: quarterly to start; can move to monthly after first 2 quarters upon request (ops lead-in required).
5) Approvals: finance ok to sign corridor up to an expected effective price uplift of ~12%; anything beyond requires VP sign-off.

Next steps:
- If this aligns, Marissa will convert to a customer-facing term sheet and we can schedule a 45-minute call to go through triggers and the operational flow.
- Please share any procurement language EdgeScale needs preemptively so we can incorporate.

Available Fri 9–11am PST for a walkthrough if that works for you.

Best,
Sean
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20261028-commit-ladder-term-sheet.xlsx, safety_corridor-draft.pdf
